title: Tropical: Enhancing SLO Attainment in Disaggregated LLM Serving via SLO-Aware Multiplexing
problem: Disaggregated LLM serving isolates prefill and decode on separate workers to optimize one phase but creates high queuing delays; non-disaggregated serving reduces queuing but causes compute interference between phases, violating latency SLOs (TTFT, TPOT).
motivation: LLM serving systems must meet strict latency SLOs for both time-to-first-token (prefill) and time-per-output-token (decode); current architectures optimize one at the cost of the other.
method: Tropical dynamically schedules the prompt-processing phase (prefill) and token-generation phase (decode) on shared workers, shifting work between them based on measured queue lengths and latencies. Instead of either permanently separating these phases onto different machines—which creates long queues—or always running them together—which causes slowdowns from interference—it adapts in real time. This balancing act lets the system simultaneously meet latency targets for both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-token (TPOT).
key_novelty: Tropical combines the benefits of disaggregated LLM serving (low interference) and non-disaggregated serving (short queues) through dynamic scheduling, simultaneously achieving both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-token (TPOT) latency targets.
contributions: 2.09x throughput improvement at 90% SLO attainment vs. state-of-the-art
9x P90 TTFT improvement over disaggregated systems with 15% P90 TPOT trade-off
2.8x P90 TPOT improvement over non-disaggregated systems at same TTFT
SLO-aware multiplexing strategy balancing queuing and interference

metrics.other: P90 TTFT 9x improvement; P90 TPOT 2.8x improvement

limitations: Evaluation on real-world datasets; hardware-specific optimizations and multi-GPU cluster scaling not detailed.
primary_theme: hybrid disaggregated LLM serving with SLO-aware multiplexing
